page: Amazon Web Services r7g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs at 1 thread per core) clocked at 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It features 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Networking operates with an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external persistent volumes for disk-reliant applications, and contains no hardware GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional RAM capabilities, with a PassMark memory score ranking in the top 10% and uncached large-block read-only and write bandwidth testing in the top 25% (209.9 GB/sec read and 97.06 GB/sec write). General compute results remain consistently in the middle 50% across Geekbench single-core (1515.0), multi-core (13031.0), and stress-ng CPU evaluations. In-memory data structures perform well, handling 26.44 million Redis SET operations per second. Tradeoffs include weak encryption throughput (bottom 25% in PassMark CPU encryption) and bottom 25% prompt processing speeds for 7B parameter models.

The Graviton architecture delivers a cost-efficient resource profile by providing high memory density and dedicated core isolation without simultaneous multithreading penalties. It is optimal for in-memory caches, distributed databases, large-scale Redis deployments, real-time analytics, and data pipeline tasks that prioritize memory throughput over GPU or specialized vector computing.
